questions.question: Which state became the first to pass a Uniform Civil Code (UCC) bill in 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttarakhand**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Uttarakhand** became the first state in independent India to pass a **Uniform Civil Code (UCC) Bill** on **February 7, 2024**.

• The bill was passed by the **Uttarakhand Legislative Assembly** following a detailed report submitted by a five-member committee headed by retired Supreme Court Judge **Ranjana Prakash Desai**.

• The primary objective of the **UCC Bill 2024** is to establish a common legal framework for **marriage, divorce, land, property, and inheritance** for all citizens, irrespective of their religion.

• A significant feature of the bill is the mandatory registration of **live-in relationships**, with failure to do so potentially leading to imprisonment or fines.

• The bill specifically excludes **Scheduled Tribes (STs)** from its application, respecting the unique traditions and customary rights of tribal communities in the state.

**Additional Information__**

• **Article 44** of the **Indian Constitution**, which is part of the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**, states that the State shall endeavor to secure for the citizens a **Uniform Civil Code** throughout the territory of India.

• While **Goa** has followed a Uniform Civil Code (the **Portuguese Civil Code of 1867**) since its liberation, **Uttarakhand** is the first state to draft and pass its own UCC legislation after India's independence.

• The **President of India**, Droupadi Murmu, gave her official assent to the **Uttarakhand Uniform Civil Code Bill** in **March 2024**, making it an Act.

• The bill prohibits **polygamy** and sets a uniform age for marriage (18 for women and 21 for men) across all communities.
</ul

questions.question: What is the primary objective of the PM-PRANAM Scheme, 2023, approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs?

options.text: To subsidize the cost of chemical fertilizers for marginal farmers
To incentivize states/UTs for reducing chemical fertilizer usage and promoting sustainability
To distribute organic farming kits directly to farmers across India
To enhance fertilizer production capacity in public sector undertakings

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To incentivize states/UTs for reducing chemical fertilizer usage and promoting sustainability**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__

• The **PM-PRANAM** (PM Programme for Restoration, Awareness, Nourishment and Amelioration of Mother Earth) scheme was approved by the **Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA)** in **June 2023**.

• The primary objective of the scheme is to incentivize **States and Union Territories** to promote the **balanced use of chemical fertilizers** and encourage the adoption of **alternative fertilizers** such as organic and bio-fertilizers.

• The scheme does not have a separate budget allocation; instead, it is funded by the **savings from the fertilizer subsidy**.

• Under this initiative, **50% of the subsidy savings** generated by a State/UT will be passed back to that State/UT as a **grant**.

• Of the grant provided, **70%** can be utilized for **asset creation** related to the technological adoption of alternative fertilizers and **30%** can be used for **incentivizing farmers**, panchayats, and self-help groups involved in awareness generation and reducing fertilizer use.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The scheme was first announced by the Union Finance Minister during the **Union Budget 2023-24**.

• The initiative aims to reduce the **fiscal burden** on the government caused by the rising cost of **fertilizer subsidies**, which have increased significantly due to global price volatility.

• It promotes **sustainable agriculture** by preventing **soil degradation** caused by the excessive and imbalanced use of chemical fertilizers like **Urea** and **DAP**.

• The scheme also supports the **GOBARdhan** initiative by promoting the use of organic manure produced from cattle waste.
</ul

questions.question: What is the name of India's space observatory that was launched to study celestial phenomena such as black holes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**AstroSat**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• **AstroSat** is India's first dedicated multi-wavelength space observatory, launched by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** on **September 28, 2015**.

• The satellite is designed to study celestial sources in **X-ray**, **optical**, and **UV spectral bands** simultaneously, which provides a unique capability to observe high-energy processes in **black holes**, **neutron stars**, and **binary star systems**.

• **Mangalyaan**, also known as the **Mars Orbiter Mission (MOM)**, was India's first interplanetary mission aimed at studying the **Martian surface** and atmosphere.

• **Chandrayaan-2** was India's second lunar exploration mission, which included an **Orbiter**, **Lander (Vikram)**, and **Rover (Pragyan)** to explore the Moon's south polar region.

• **RISAT-1** (Radar Imaging Satellite-1) is an indigenous **Earth observation satellite** that uses Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) for applications in agriculture, forestry, and disaster management.

**Additional Information__**

• **AstroSat** was launched into a 650 km orbit with an inclination of 6 degrees by the **PSLV-C30** rocket from **Sriharikota**.

• It carries five major scientific payloads: **UVIT** (Ultra Violet Imaging Telescope), **SXT** (Soft X-ray Telescope), **LAXPC** (Large Area X-ray Proportional Counter), **CZTI** (Cadmium Zinc Telluride Imager), and **SSM** (Scanning Sky Monitor).

• India is the **fifth country/agency** in the world to launch a full-fledged space observatory, following the **USA (NASA)**, **Russia**, **Japan**, and the **European Space Agency (ESA)**.

• In 2024, ISRO also launched **XPoSat** (X-ray Polarimeter Satellite) to further study the polarization of cosmic X-rays from sources like **black holes**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following organisms does not reproduce through spore formation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Yeast fungus**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Yeast** is a unicellular fungus that primarily reproduces through an asexual process called **Budding**. In this process, a small bulb-like projection, called a **bud**, comes out from the yeast cell, grows, and eventually detaches to form a new organism.

• **Penicillium fungus** reproduces asexually through the formation of specialized spores called **conidia** (or conidiospores).

• **Rhizopus fungus**, commonly known as **bread mold**, reproduces through **spore formation**. It develops **sporangia** at the tips of hyphae, which burst to release thousands of tiny spores into the air.

• **Micro fungi** (a general term for microscopic fungi) like **Mucor** or **Aspergillus** also typically utilize **spore formation** as their primary mode of asexual reproduction.

• Therefore, among the given options, **Yeast** is the organism that does not use spore formation as its primary asexual reproductive method, relying instead on **budding**.

**Additional Information__**

• **Asexual reproduction** is a mode of reproduction that does not involve the fusion of gametes or change in the number of chromosomes. Common types include **Binary Fission**, **Fragmentation**, **Regeneration**, **Budding**, and **Spore Formation**.

• **Spores** are thick-walled resistant structures that can withstand unfavorable conditions like high temperature and low humidity, allowing the fungus to survive until conditions become favorable for growth.

• **Saccharomyces cerevisiae** is the most common species of **Yeast** used in baking and brewing due to its ability to ferment sugars into carbon dioxide and ethanol.

• While some yeasts can form spores (ascospores) under extreme stress, **Budding** remains their defining and most common characteristic in biological classification questions regarding reproductive modes.
</ul

questions.question: The Deccan Traps were formed as a result of which geological event?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Volcanic eruptions**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Deccan Traps** are a massive **Large Igneous Province** located in west-central India. They were formed by the accumulation of multiple layers of solidified **flood basalt** resulting from intense volcanic activity.

• The primary geological event responsible for their formation was a series of **fissure-type volcanic eruptions**. These occurred as the **Indian Plate** moved over the **Reunion hotspot** in the **Indian Ocean** during its northward drift.

• **Earthquakes** are seismic vibrations caused by the sudden release of energy in the Earth's lithosphere. While they occur in volcanic regions, they do not deposit the massive layers of igneous rock that define the Deccan plateau. **Hence, this option is incorrect.**

• **Volcanic eruptions** involved the outpouring of low-viscosity **basaltic lava** that spread over vast areas, cooling to form the characteristic step-like topography of the region. **Hence, this option is correct.**

• **Glacial movement** refers to the flow of ice masses which shapes the landscape through erosion and the deposition of sediments like **moraines**. The Deccan region shows no evidence of massive glaciation during the **Mesozoic Era**. **Hence, this option is incorrect.**

• **Tectonic plate collision** is responsible for orogenic events, such as the formation of the **Himalayas** when the **Indian Plate** collided with the **Eurasian Plate**. However, the Deccan Traps are volcanic in origin and were formed before the main collision event. **Hence, this option is incorrect.**

**Additional Information__**
__

• The term **'Trap'** is derived from the **Swedish** word **'Trappa'**, which translates to **'stairs'**. This refers to the step-like or terraced appearance of the hills in the **Western Ghats**.

• Geographically, the traps cover a significant portion of India, primarily in the states of **Maharashtra**, **Gujarat**, and **Madhya Pradesh**, with smaller extensions into **Karnataka** and **Telangana**.

• The weathering of these volcanic basaltic rocks over millions of years has led to the formation of fertile **Black Soil**, also known as **Regur soil**.

• This **Black Soil** is highly valued for its moisture-retention capacity and is the primary soil type used for **Cotton** cultivation in the **Deccan** region.

• The total thickness of the lava flows varies across the region but reaches its maximum of over **2,000 meters** in the western part, particularly near the **Mumbai** coast.

**Important Points__**

• The eruptions took place approximately **66 million years ago**, coinciding with the end of the **Cretaceous period** and the beginning of the **Paleogene period**.

• Scientific research suggests that the massive release of volcanic gases, such as **carbon dioxide** and **sulfur dioxide**, during these eruptions contributed to global climate change and the **K-Pg mass extinction** event, which saw the end of the dinosaurs.

• The lava is primarily classified as **Tholeiitic basalt**, which is rich in iron and magnesium and has a low silica content, allowing it to flow easily over hundreds of kilometers.

• The **Deccan Traps** are one of the few examples of a continental flood basalt province on Earth, comparable in scale to the **Siberian Traps** in **Russia**.

• The volcanic activity is estimated to have lasted for a duration ranging from **30,000 to 1,000,000 years**, occurring in several distinct pulses of high-volume eruptions.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is a practical example of convection?

options.text: Warming your hands by a fire

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Heating water on a stove**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Convection** is the mode of heat transfer that takes place in **fluids** (liquids and gases) through the actual movement of the particles of the medium.

• When **heating water on a stove**, the water at the bottom of the container gets heated, its density decreases, and it rises. The cooler, denser water from the top moves down to replace it, creating **convection currents** that distribute heat throughout the liquid.

• **Warming your hands by a fire** is primarily an example of **Radiation**, as the heat is felt even without direct contact or a moving fluid medium between the fire and the hands (though some convection occurs if hands are held directly above the fire).

• **Heat transmission through a vacuum** is only possible via **Radiation**. Convection and conduction both require a material medium to transfer energy.

• **Heat transfer in metal** occurs through **Conduction**. In solids, heat is transferred from one molecule to another through vibrations and the movement of free electrons without the bulk movement of the material itself.

**Additional Information__**

• There are three primary modes of heat transfer: **Conduction**, **Convection**, and **Radiation**.

• **Natural Convection** occurs due to **buoyancy forces** (differences in density caused by temperature variations), such as **Sea breezes** and **Land breezes**.

• **Forced Convection** occurs when a fluid is forced to flow over a surface by external means like a **fan**, **pump**, or **suction device**.

• The rate of heat transfer in convection is often described by **Newtons Law of Cooling**.

• **Radiation** is the only method that can transfer heat through the **vacuum of space**, which is how thermal energy from the **Sun** reaches the Earth.
</ul

questions.question: What type of accounts are opened under the PMJDY scheme?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Savings Accounts**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)** is a **National Mission for Financial Inclusion** launched to ensure that every household in **India** has access to at least one basic banking account. The accounts opened under this scheme are **Savings Accounts**, specifically categorized as **Basic Savings Bank Deposit Accounts (BSBDA)**.

• These **Savings Accounts** are designed as **Zero Balance Accounts**, meaning there is no requirement for the account holder to maintain a minimum balance, which is a significant departure from regular savings accounts in commercial banks. **Hence, the correct answer is Savings Accounts.**

• The scheme was officially launched on **28th August 2014** by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** with the objective of integrating the unbanked population into the formal financial system.

• Other options like **Fixed Deposit Accounts** and **Recurring Deposit Accounts** are not the primary accounts under **PMJDY** because they are term-based investment products where money is locked for a specific duration. **Current Accounts** are also incorrect as they are meant for **Business Entities** and **Traders**, usually requiring high minimum balances and offering no interest on deposits.

• The **Savings Accounts** under **PMJDY** provide the necessary liquidity for low-income groups, allowing them to deposit and withdraw small amounts of money frequently while earning interest on their savings.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **RuPay Debit Card**: Every **PMJDY** account holder is provided with a **RuPay Debit Card**, which can be used at **ATMs** and **PoS** terminals across the country. This card also includes a built-in **Accident Insurance Cover**.

• **Insurance Benefits**: Initially, the **Accident Insurance Cover** was **Rs. 1 lakh**, but for accounts opened after **28th August 2018**, this benefit was increased to **Rs. 2 lakh**. Additionally, a **Life Insurance Cover** of **Rs. 30,000** was provided to eligible beneficiaries who opened accounts during the initial phase.

• **Overdraft Facility**: To provide credit access to the poor, an **Overdraft (OD) facility** of up to **Rs. 10,000** is available to eligible account holders after **6 months** of satisfactory account operation. The age limit for availing this facility is **18 to 65 years**.

• **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)**: **PMJDY** accounts serve as the primary channel for **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)**, ensuring that government subsidies for **LPG (PAHAL)**, **MGNREGA** wages, and **Pensions** are credited directly into the beneficiaries' accounts, eliminating middlemen and leakages.

• **Slogan**: The mission operates under the inspiring slogan **'Mera Khata, Bhagya Vidhata'**, which translates to **'My Account, My Destiny Maker'**.

**Important Points__**

• **Eligibility**: Any **Indian Citizen** above the **age of 10 years** is eligible to open a **PMJDY** account. The scheme focuses on the **Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile (JAM)** trinity to strengthen the financial infrastructure.

• **Simplified KYC**: To ensure maximum participation, the **Government of India** introduced simplified **KYC** norms. Individuals without official valid documents can open **'Small Accounts'**, which have certain limitations on total credits and withdrawals but allow immediate entry into the banking fold.

• **PMJDY 2.0**: In **2018**, the government extended the program indefinitely and shifted the focus from **'Every Household'** to **'Every Unbanked Adult'**, further deepening the reach of financial services in rural and semi-urban areas.

• **Statistical Impact**: As of **2023**, more than **50 crore** accounts have been opened under the scheme, with more than **55 percent** of these accounts belonging to **Women** and nearly **67 percent** opened in **Rural and Semi-Urban** areas.

• **Implementation**: The scheme is monitored and implemented by the **Department of Financial Services** under the **Ministry of Finance**. It has been recognized by the **Guinness World Records** for the most bank accounts opened in one week as part of a financial inclusion campaign.
</ul

questions.question: What is the role of rainwater harvesting in the Jal Shakti Abhiyan?

options.text: To store excess rainwater for future use

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To store excess rainwater for future use**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The **Jal Shakti Abhiyan (JSA)** was launched by the **Government of India** in **2019** as a time-bound, mission-mode campaign to promote **water conservation** and **water security** across the country.

• The primary role of **rainwater harvesting** in this initiative is to collect and **store excess rainwater** during the **monsoon** season, ensuring that this water is available for **future use** during dry periods and to **recharge groundwater** aquifers. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***

• The mission aims to combat **groundwater depletion** by replenishing underground water tables through scientific conservation methods, rather than increasing the rate of depletion. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

• While the campaign is implemented in both **rural** and **urban** areas, its core objective is **water sustainability** and ecological restoration, not the promotion of **urbanization**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

• The **Jal Shakti Abhiyan** actually supports and enhances **agricultural activities** by providing reliable water sources for irrigation through **watershed development** and **water harvesting**, rather than reducing them. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**

__

• The **Ministry of Jal Shakti** was established in **May 2019** by merging the **Ministry of Water Resources, River Development & Ganga Rejuvenation** and the **Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation** to provide a unified approach to water management.

• The **Catch the Rain** campaign, launched under the **National Water Mission**, uses the tagline **Catch the rain, where it falls, when it falls** to encourage the creation of **Rain Water Harvesting Structures (RWHS)** suitable to the climatic conditions of various regions.

• The initiative initially targeted **256 water-stressed districts** and **1,592 water-stressed blocks** across **India**, focusing on urgent interventions to prevent a severe water crisis.

• Key intervention areas of the **Jal Shakti Abhiyan** include **renovation of traditional water bodies** (such as tanks and ponds), **reuse and recharge structures**, **watershed development**, and **intensive afforestation**.

• The campaign is designed as a **Jan Andolan** (People's Movement), emphasizing **community participation** and awareness to make water conservation a part of daily life for every citizen.

**Important Points__**

• **Rainwater harvesting** techniques promoted under the mission include **rooftop rainwater harvesting** for buildings, **percolation pits**, **check dams**, and **recharge wells** to maximize the absorption of water into the soil.

• The mission leverages funds and labor from the **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)** to construct and maintain water conservation infrastructure in rural areas.

• The **Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the Rain 2024** campaign focuses on the theme **Sustainablity of Ground Water Sources for Drinking Water**, highlighting the critical need to protect drinking water sources.

• The **Central Nodal Officers (CNOs)** and **Technical Officers** from the **Central Government** visit districts to coordinate with **District Collectors** and ensure the effective implementation of water-saving measures.

• **Data** from the **Central Ground Water Board (CGWB)** is used to identify priority areas where the **water table** has fallen significantly, ensuring that resources are directed where they are most needed.
</ul

questions.question: Which Indian company is managing the operations of Chabahar Port?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Ports Global Limited (IPGL)**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Indian Ports Global Limited (IPGL)** is the specialized entity established by the Government of India to develop and operate the **Shahid Beheshti terminal** of the **Chabahar Port** in **Iran**.

• IPGL was originally formed as a joint venture between **Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust (JNPT)** and **Deendayal Port Trust** (formerly Kandla Port Trust) to facilitate India's strategic investments in overseas ports.

• In **May 2024**, a historic **10-year long-term contract** was signed between **IPGL** and the **Port and Maritime Organisation (PMO)** of Iran, ensuring continuous Indian management of the terminal.

• The primary objective of managing this port is to create a reliable trade route to **Afghanistan** and **Central Asian countries**, bypassing the land route through **Pakistan**.

• While **JNPT** is a stakeholder in the venture, the direct operational management is handled by the dedicated subsidiary, **IPGL**.

**Additional Information__**

• **Chabahar Port** is located on the **Gulf of Oman** in southeastern Iran and is the only Iranian port with direct access to the **Indian Ocean**.

• The port is a crucial link in the **International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC)**, a multi-modal transportation network connecting India, Iran, Azerbaijan, and Russia.

• Strategically, Chabahar is seen as a counter to the **Gwadar Port** in Pakistan, which is being developed by **China** as part of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC).

• The **Shipping Corporation of India (SCI)** handles maritime logistics but does not manage the port operations, and **Adani Ports** is a private entity not currently managing the state-led Chabahar project.
</ul

questions.question: Which two regions does the IMEC alliance aim to connect through the Middle East?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Asia and Europe**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC)** is a landmark infrastructure project aimed at connecting **India (Asia)** to **Europe** through the **Middle East**.

• The project was officially announced on the sidelines of the **G20 Summit** held in **New Delhi** in **September 2023**.

• The primary objective of the IMEC alliance is to stimulate economic development through enhanced connectivity and economic integration between **Asia**, the **Persian Gulf**, and **Europe**.

• The corridor is designed to include a **railway network**, **ship-to-rail transit**, and other transport routes to facilitate the efficient movement of goods and services.

• Signatory nations and entities include **India**, the **United States**, **Saudi Arabia**, the **United Arab Emirates (UAE)**, **France**, **Germany**, **Italy**, and the **European Union**.

**Additional Information__**

• The IMEC consists of two distinct corridors: the **East Corridor**, which connects **India** to the **Arabian Gulf**, and the **Northern Corridor**, which connects the **Arabian Gulf** to **Europe**.

• In addition to transport infrastructure, the project envisions laying **undersea cables** for **digital connectivity** and pipelines for **clean hydrogen** exports.

• The initiative is often viewed as a strategic alternative to China's **Belt and Road Initiative (BRI)**, aiming to provide a more transparent and sustainable infrastructure model.

• The corridor is expected to reduce shipping costs and transit time significantly, enhancing trade efficiency between **South Asia** and **European markets**.
</ul

questions.question: What is the main focus of the Happiness Index?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Measuring happiness and wellbeing**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **World Happiness Report** is an annual publication that ranks **156 countries** based on how happy their citizens perceive themselves to be, with the primary focus on **measuring happiness and wellbeing**. *Hence, the statement 'Measuring happiness and wellbeing' is correct.*

• The index uses **subjective wellbeing** data to complement traditional objective indicators like **GDP** or **employment rates**, providing a more comprehensive view of **social progress**.

• The ranking is determined by six key variables: **GDP per capita**, **social support** (having someone to count on in times of trouble), **healthy life expectancy** at birth, **freedom to make life choices**, **generosity** (measured by recent donations), and **perceptions of corruption** in government and business.

• **Tracking population growth** is the primary function of **demographic surveys** and **national censuses**, which focus on **birth rates**, **death rates**, and **migration** rather than emotional wellbeing. *Hence, the statement 'Tracking population growth' is incorrect.*

• **Calculating government incoming** refers to **fiscal policy** and **revenue collection** metrics, which are monitored by **central banks** and **ministries of finance** to manage the **national budget**. *Hence, the statement 'Calculating government incoming' is incorrect.*

• **Checking school performance** involves educational assessments such as the **Program for International Student Assessment (PISA)** or **literacy rate** surveys, which evaluate **academic outcomes** rather than general life satisfaction. *Hence, the statement 'Checking school performance' is incorrect.*

**Additional Information__**
__

• The **World Happiness Report** is published by the **United Nations Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)** and was first released in **April 2012**.

• The report was launched to support the **United Nations High-Level Meeting on Happiness and Well-being**, following a **2011** **UN General Assembly** resolution inviting member countries to measure the happiness of their people.

• The data for the rankings comes primarily from the **Gallup World Poll**, which utilizes the **Cantril ladder** question: respondents are asked to think of a ladder, with the best possible life for them being a **10** and the worst possible life being a **0**.

• The concept of prioritizing happiness over economic indicators was pioneered by **Bhutan** in the **1970s**, when the **4th King**, **Jigme Singye Wangchuck**, introduced the **Gross National Happiness (GNH)** index as a more important metric than **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**.

• **Nordic countries**, such as **Finland**, **Denmark**, **Iceland**, and **Norway**, consistently dominate the top of the index due to high levels of **social trust**, **low corruption**, and **effective welfare states**.

**Important Points__**

• In the **World Happiness Report 2024**, **Finland** was ranked as the happiest country in the world for the **seventh consecutive year**.

• **India** was ranked **126th** out of **143 countries** in the **2024** report, indicating that despite **economic growth**, there are significant challenges in **social support** and **perceived freedom**.

• The **2024** report also highlighted a **happiness gap** based on **age**, noting that in some regions, **younger populations** are reporting lower levels of happiness compared to **older generations** due to **social media** pressures and **economic instability**.

• The index serves as a critical tool for **policymakers** to shift the focus of **public policy** toward **mental health**, **community building**, and **environmental sustainability**.
</ul

questions.question: What is the term for the situation where demand exceeds supply in a market?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shortage**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• A **Shortage**, also referred to as **excess demand**, is an economic state where the **quantity demanded** by consumers for a specific product or service is significantly higher than the **quantity supplied** by producers at the current **market price**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Shortage.***

• In a **free market**, a shortage typically occurs when the price of an item is set **below the equilibrium level**. Because the price is low, more people want to buy the good, but businesses find it less profitable to produce or sell it, creating a **market imbalance**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***

• A **Surplus** is the exact opposite of a shortage; it occurs when the **quantity supplied** exceeds the **quantity demanded**, usually because the price is **above the equilibrium point**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

• **Equilibrium** is the condition where **market forces** are balanced. At the **equilibrium price**, the amount of goods buyers want to buy is exactly equal to the amount of goods sellers want to sell, resulting in no **shortage** or **surplus**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

• **Deflation** refers to a general **decrease in the price level** of goods and services across an entire economy over a specific period. It is a **macroeconomic** phenomenon related to the **purchasing power** of money rather than a specific supply-demand mismatch in a single market. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Price Ceilings and Shortages**: Governments sometimes implement a **Price Ceiling**, which is a **legal maximum price**. If this ceiling is set below the **natural equilibrium price**, it leads to a persistent **shortage** because prices cannot rise to clear the market. A classic example is **Rent Control** in cities like **New York** or **Mumbai**.

• **Market Mechanisms**: According to the **Law of Supply and Demand**, if a shortage exists, **market competition** among buyers will naturally drive the price up. As the price increases, the **quantity demanded** decreases and the **quantity supplied** increases until they meet at **equilibrium**.

• **Causes of Shortages**: Shortages can be caused by various factors including **supply chain disruptions**, **natural disasters**, **government regulations**, or sudden **shifts in consumer preferences**. For instance, the **Global Chip Shortage** that began in **2020** severely impacted the **automobile** and **electronics industries**.

• **Economic Impacts**: When a **shortage** occurs, it often leads to **rationing**, **long waiting lines** (queues), and the potential development of **black markets** where goods are traded illegally at prices much higher than the **official rate**.

• **Inventory Management**: In the **retail sector**, a shortage is often called a **stockout**. Modern businesses use **Just-in-Time (JIT)** inventory systems to keep costs low, but this makes them more vulnerable to **shortages** if there is a sudden **logistical delay** or **demand spike**.

**Important Points__**

• **Invisible Hand**: The concept introduced by **Adam Smith** in **1776** suggests that the **price mechanism** acts as an invisible hand that resolves **shortages** and **surpluses** automatically in a **laissez-faire** economy.

• **Elasticity**: The duration and severity of a **shortage** often depend on the **Price Elasticity of Demand**. If a good is a **necessity** (like medicine or basic food), a shortage can lead to drastic **price hikes** because consumers cannot easily reduce their consumption.

• **Historical Example**: The **1973 Oil Crisis** is a famous example of a global **shortage**. Following an **embargo** by **OPEC**, the supply of **petroleum** dropped sharply, leading to massive **price increases** and **fuel rationing** in many **Western countries**.
</ul

questions.question: Which issue does the Beti Bachao Beti Padhao Yojana primarily address?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Female literacy and welfare**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP)** was launched by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** on **22 January 2015** at **Panipat, Haryana**.

• The scheme primarily addresses **Female literacy and welfare** by ensuring the survival, protection, and education of the girl child. It aims to eliminate gender-biased sex-selective practices and promote the value of the girl child. ***Hence, option 4 is correct.***

• It was initiated in response to the declining **Child Sex Ratio (CSR)** in **India**, which had dropped from **927** in **2001** to **918** in the **2011 Census**.

• The scheme is a tri-ministerial effort involving the **Ministry of Women and Child Development**, the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare**, and the **Ministry of Education** (formerly **Human Resource Development**).

• While **Women's employment** (Option 1) is a critical issue, it is not the primary focus of BBBP, as other schemes like **STEP (Support to Training and Employment Programme for Women)** are specifically designed for that purpose. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***

• **Child marriage** (Option 2) is a legal and social issue addressed primarily by the **Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006**, although BBBP indirectly supports this by encouraging girls to stay in school. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***

• **Gender-based discrimination** (Option 3) is the broad underlying theme the scheme fights against, but the specific operational objectives are focused on the literacy and welfare of the girl child. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• The **Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY)** was launched as a companion scheme to BBBP to encourage parents to save for the **higher education** and **marriage** expenses of their girl children.

• The scheme was initially launched in **100 districts** with low **CSR** and was later expanded to all **640 districts** of **India** in **March 2018** during an event in **Jhunjhunu, Rajasthan**.

• Strict enforcement of the **Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act, 1994** is a core component of the scheme to prevent **female foeticide**.

• **National Girl Child Day** is celebrated every year on **24 January** to spread awareness about the rights of girls and the importance of their **health** and **nutrition**.

• The scheme uses the tagline **'Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao'**, which translates to **'Save the girl child, educate the girl child'**, emphasizing its dual focus on survival and literacy.

**Important Points__**

• The **long-term objectives** of the scheme include improving the **Sex Ratio at Birth (SRB)** and ensuring **100% enrollment** of girls in **secondary education**.

• The scheme targets three groups: **Primary** (pregnant and lactating mothers, parents), **Secondary** (youth, adolescents, doctors, private clinics), and **Tertiary** (officials, PRIs, media, and religious leaders).

• **Digital Guddi Gudda Boards** have been set up in various districts to display birth statistics (number of girls born vs. boys) in public places like **Panchayat offices** to foster community pride.

• The scheme also focuses on providing **functional toilets for girls** in all schools to reduce dropout rates and improve **female literacy**.

• Since its inception in **2015**, several districts have reported a significant improvement in the **Sex Ratio at Birth**, showcasing the positive impact of the **BBBP** initiative.
</ul

questions.question: What is the primary goal of the Jal Jeevan Mission?

options.text: Providing piped drinking water to households

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Providing piped drinking water to households**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM)** is a flagship program of the **Government of India**, launched by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** on **August 15, 2019**, during the **73rd Independence Day** speech.

• The primary goal of the mission is to provide **Functional Household Tap Connections (FHTC)** to every rural household in the country by the year **2024**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***

• The mission ensures the supply of **55 liters of water per capita per day (lpcd)** of prescribed quality (as per **BIS:10500** standards) on a regular and long-term basis.

• **River conservation** is primarily managed under the **Namami Gange Programme** and the **National River Conservation Plan (NRCP)**, rather than the Jal Jeevan Mission. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

• **Irrigation system modernization** is the core objective of the **Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY)**, which aims to improve on-farm water use efficiency. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

• While **groundwater recharge** is a component of source sustainability within JJM, it is the primary focus of the **Atal Bhujal Yojana**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• The **Jal Jeevan Mission** is implemented by the **Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation** under the **Ministry of Jal Shakti**.

• The funding pattern for the mission is shared between the **Centre** and **States** in the ratio of **90:10** for **Himalayan and North-Eastern States**, **50:50** for other states, and **100%** for **Union Territories**.

• **Goa** became the first **Har Ghar Jal** state in **India** by providing **100%** tap water connections to all rural households, followed by **Telangana** and **Haryana**.

• **Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu** became the first **Har Ghar Jal** Union Territory in the country.

• The mission also focuses on **integrated demand and supply-side management** of water at the local level, including **rainwater harvesting** and **greywater management** (domestic wastewater treatment for reuse in agriculture).

**Important Points__**

• The mission is a **community-led movement** involving **Panchayati Raj Institutions** and **Village Water and Sanitation Committees (VWSC)**, often referred to as **Pani Samitis**, which play a key role in planning, implementation, and management.

• In **2021**, the **Jal Jeevan Mission (Urban)** was launched to provide universal coverage of water supply through functional taps in all **4,378 Statutory Towns**, aligning with **Sustainable Development Goal 6 (SDG 6)**.

• The program emphasizes **Water Quality Monitoring and Surveillance (WQMS)**, encouraging the use of **Field Test Kits (FTKs)** by community members, especially women, to test water samples for contamination.

• As of **2023-2024**, the mission has significantly increased rural tap water coverage from approximately **17%** in **2019** to over **75%** nationwide, showcasing rapid infrastructure development.

• The **Jal Jeevan Survekshan** is an annual assessment conducted to rank districts and states based on their performance in implementing the mission goals.
</ul

questions.question: Name the state having the highest literacy rate according to the 2011 Census?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• According to the **2011 Census**, **Kerala** emerged as the state with the highest literacy rate in **India**, recording a remarkable **94.00%**. This achievement is attributed to long-standing social reforms, a strong emphasis on primary education, and various state-led literacy missions.

• The gender-wise breakup of literacy in **Kerala** shows that **male literacy** stands at **96.11%**, while **female literacy** is at **92.07%**. This narrow gender gap highlights the state's success in promoting inclusive education.

• In comparison to other options, **Tamil Nadu** recorded a literacy rate of **80.09%**, **Maharashtra** stood at **82.34%**, and **Gujarat** had a literacy rate of **78.03%** during the **2011 Census**. None of these states surpassed the benchmark set by **Kerala**.

• The **2011 Census** data revealed that **Bihar** had the lowest literacy rate in the country at **61.80%**, followed by **Arunachal Pradesh** at **65.38%** and **Rajasthan** at **66.11%**.

• The high literacy in **Kerala** is a result of historical initiatives like the **Total Literacy Campaign** launched in **Ernakulam** in **1989**, which eventually made it the first district in **India** to achieve **100% literacy**.

**Additional Information__**

• The **Census of 2011** was the **15th National Census** of **India** since **1872** and the **7th** after **Independence**. It was conducted under the **Census Act of 1948**.

• The overall **literacy rate** of **India** in **2011** was **74.04%**. The **male literacy rate** was **82.14%**, and the **female literacy rate** was **65.46%**.

• Among **Union Territories**, **Lakshadweep** held the highest literacy rate at **91.85%**, while **Dadra and Nagar Haveli** recorded the lowest at **76.24%**.

• For the purpose of the **Census**, a person aged **7 years and above** who can both **read and write** with understanding in any language is considered **literate**. A person who can only read but cannot write is not considered literate.

• Other top-performing states in terms of literacy include **Mizoram** at **91.33%**, **Goa** at **88.70%**, and **Tripura** at **87.22%**. These states have shown significant progress in human development indices.

• The **Registrar General and Census Commissioner** of **India**, under the **Ministry of Home Affairs**, is responsible for conducting the decennial census. The **2011 Census** commissioner was **C. Chandramouli**.
</ul

questions.question: What is the tenure of a Governor in an Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5 years**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The tenure of the **Governor** of an **Indian state** is governed by **Article 156** of the **Constitution of India**. According to this article, the **Governor** shall hold office for a term of **5 years** from the date on which they enter their office. *Hence, the statement regarding the 5-year term is correct.*

• The **Governor** holds office during the **pleasure of the President**. This means that the **President of India** has the authority to remove a **Governor** at any time before the completion of the **5-year** term without assigning any specific reason.

• A **Governor** may, by writing under their hand addressed to the **President**, resign from their office at any point during their tenure.

• Notwithstanding the expiration of the **5-year** term, the **Governor** shall continue to hold office until their successor enters upon their office to ensure there is no constitutional vacuum in the state administration.

• The option of **3 years** is incorrect as there is no such provision in the **Constitution** for the **Governor**. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*

• The option of **6 years** is incorrect because this duration typically applies to members of the **Rajya Sabha** and the **State Legislative Council**, or the **Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)**, but not to the **Governor**. *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*

• The option **Until retirement** is incorrect because the **Constitution** does not prescribe a retirement age for the **Governor**, unlike judges of the **Supreme Court** (**65 years**) or **High Court** (**62 years**). *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Constitutional Position**: **Article 153** mandates that there shall be a **Governor** for each state. However, the **7th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1956** made it possible to appoint the same person as **Governor** for **two or more states**.

• **Appointment**: The **Governor** is not elected but is appointed by the **President** by warrant under his hand and seal as per **Article 155**. This ensures the **Union Government** maintains a degree of control over state administration.

• **Qualifications**: To be eligible for the post of **Governor** under **Article 157**, a person must be a **citizen of India** and must have completed the age of **35 years**. Additionally, they should not hold any **office of profit** and should not be a member of either **House of Parliament** or a **State Legislature**.

• **Executive Powers**: The **Governor** is the **Constitutional Head** of the state. All executive actions of the **State Government** are formally taken in their name. They appoint the **Chief Minister** and, on the **Chief Minister’s** advice, other ministers.

• **Legislative Powers**: The **Governor** has the power to summon or prorogue the **State Legislature** and dissolve the **State Legislative Assembly**. They also address the first session of the **State Legislature** after each **general election** and at the commencement of the first session of each **year**.

**Important Points__**

• **Judicial Immunity**: Under **Article 361**, the **Governor** enjoys personal immunity from legal liability for their official acts. During their term of office, no criminal proceedings can be instituted against them, and they cannot be arrested or imprisoned.

• **Sarkaria Commission (1983)**: This commission recommended that the **Governor’s** **5-year** term should not be disturbed except for extremely compelling reasons. It suggested that the **Governor** should be an eminent person from outside the state and not intimately connected with local politics.

• **Punchhi Commission (2007)**: This commission on **Centre-State Relations** suggested that the phrase **during the pleasure of the President** should be deleted from the **Constitution** because it leads to the arbitrary removal of **Governors**. It recommended a fixed tenure of **5 years** with a provision for **impeachment** by the **State Legislature**.

• **Discretionary Powers**: Unlike the **President**, the **Governor** has certain **discretionary powers**, such as recommending the imposition of **President’s Rule** (**Article 356**) in the state or reserving certain bills for the consideration of the **President** (**Article 200**).

• **Oath of Office**: The oath of office to the **Governor** is administered by the **Chief Justice** of the concerned **State High Court** or, in their absence, the senior-most judge of that court.

57:T

questions.question: Bihu songs are a part of which Indian state's folk tradition?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Bihu songs**, known as **Bihu Geet**, are a core component of the folk tradition of **Assam**, a state in **Northeast India**. These songs are performed during the **Bihu festival**, which is the most important cultural celebration for the **Assamese community**.

• The songs are traditionally characterized by themes of **love**, **eroticism**, **nature**, and the **agricultural cycle**. They reflect the joys and sorrows of the rural life of **Assam**.

• **Bihu songs** are accompanied by the **Bihu dance**, which involves energetic steps and rapid hand movements. This folk tradition is inclusive, performed by both young men and women in the open fields or **Bakori**.

• The musical accompaniment for these songs includes traditional instruments like the **Dhol** (a percussion instrument), **Pepa** (a hornpipe made from buffalo horn), **Gogona** (a reed/bamboo instrument), **Toka** (a bamboo clapper), and **Bahi** (flute).

• The tradition is deeply rooted in the **fertility cult**, where the music and dance are believed to stimulate the **earth's fertility** and ensure a **bountiful harvest**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Assam.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Punjab**: This northern state is famous for folk traditions like **Bhangra** and **Gidda**. **Bhangra** is typically performed by men during the **Baisakhi** festival to celebrate the harvest, while **Gidda** is a graceful dance performed by women.

• **Gujarat**: Known for its vibrant folk dances such as **Garba** and **Dandiya Raas**, which are performed extensively during the **Navratri** festival. These traditions involve circular movements and the use of sticks (Dandiya) to honor **Goddess Durga**.

• **Odisha**: This state is home to the classical dance **Odissi** and various folk traditions like **Sambalpuri**, **Chhau**, and **Ghumura**. **Sambalpuri** songs and dances are particularly famous for their rhythmic beats and the use of the **Mahuri** and **Dhol**.

• **Assam's Three Bihus**: The state celebrates three types of Bihu in a **year**. **Bohag Bihu** (or **Rongali Bihu**) in **April** marks the **Assamese New Year**; **Kati Bihu** (or **Kongali Bihu**) in **October** is a more solemn observation related to crop protection; and **Magh Bihu** (or **Bhogali Bihu**) in **January** is a harvest festival centered around feasting.

**Important Points__**

• In **April 2023**, **Assam** created a **Guinness World Record** when over **11,000** dancers and drummers performed the **Bihu dance** and played the **Dhol** at the **Sarusajai Stadium** in **Guwahati**.

• The **Pepa**, an essential instrument in **Bihu songs**, is traditionally crafted from the horn of a **dead buffalo**, and its piercing sound is synonymous with the **spring season** in **Assam**.

• **Bihu Geet** are often composed in **couplets** that rhyme, making them easy to improvise and pass down through **oral tradition** across **generations**.

• The **Government of India** and the **Sangeet Natak Akademi** actively promote **Bihu** as a vital part of India's **intangible cultural heritage**.
</ul

questions.question: What is the name given to the points scored in a basketball game?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Point**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• In the sport of **Basketball**, the scoring system is based on the accumulation of **Points**. A team wins the game by scoring more points than their opponent within the designated playing time. ***Hence, the correct answer is Point.***

• A **Field Goal** is the most common way to score and is worth **2 points** if the ball is thrown from within the **Three-point arc**.

• A **Three-pointer** is awarded when a player successfully shoots the ball into the basket from beyond the **Three-point line**, which is a semi-circular arc on the court. This shot grants the team **3 points**.

• A **Free Throw** is an uncontested scoring opportunity awarded to a player after certain types of fouls are committed by the opposing team. Each successful free throw is worth **1 point**.

• The other options provided are incorrect for basketball: **Goal** is the scoring unit for sports like **Football (Soccer)**, **Hockey**, and **Handball**; **Run** is the scoring unit used in **Cricket** and **Baseball**; and **Touchdown** is the primary scoring method in **American Football**, worth **6 points**.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Basketball** was invented by **Dr. James Naismith**, a Canadian physical education instructor, in **December 1891** in **Springfield, Massachusetts**, **USA**.

• The **National Basketball Association (NBA)**, which is the premier professional basketball league in the **United States** and **Canada**, officially adopted the **Three-point line** during the **1979-1980 season**.

• The **International Basketball Federation (FIBA)** is the world governing body for the sport. It was founded in **1932** and is responsible for organizing international competitions like the **FIBA Basketball World Cup** and the **Olympic Basketball Tournament**.

• The standard height of the **Basketball Rim** (the hoop) is exactly **10 feet** (or **3.05 meters**) above the floor, a measurement that has remained constant since the game's inception.

• The **Shot Clock** was introduced to the **NBA** in **1954** (set at **24 seconds**) to prevent teams from stalling and to increase the number of scoring opportunities, thereby making the game more exciting for spectators.

**Important Points__**

• The record for the most **Points** scored by a single player in an **NBA** game is **100**, set by **Wilt Chamberlain** of the **Philadelphia Warriors** on **March 2, 1962**.

• In modern basketball, **LeBron James** holds the record for the highest **All-time leading scorer** in **NBA** history, surpassing the long-standing record of **Kareem Abdul-Jabbar** in **2023**.

• Basketball games cannot end in a draw. If the score is tied at the end of regulation time, the teams play **Overtime** periods (usually **5 minutes** in the **NBA** and **FIBA**) until a winner is decided.

• The **Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame**, located in **Springfield**, serves as the primary library and museum dedicated to the history and great players of the sport.
</ul

questions.question: Mulk Raj Anand is known for writing about:

options.text: Indian rural life and social issues

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian rural life and social issues**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mulk Raj Anand** (**1905–2004**) was a pioneering Indian novelist, short-story writer, and art critic who wrote in **English**. He is best known for his realistic and sympathetic portrayal of the **underprivileged** and the **downtrodden** in Indian society.
 
• His literary career was deeply influenced by his **socialist** leanings and his direct observation of the **poverty** and **suffering** in **rural India**. He broke away from the traditional romanticized view of India to present a **realistic** picture of **social injustice**.
 
• His debut novel, **Untouchable**, published in **1935**, is a landmark in Indian literature. It depicts a single day in the life of **Bakha**, a young "sweeper," who is a victim of the **caste system**. This work highlighted the **humanity** of those deemed "polluted" by society.
 
• In **1936**, he published **Coolie**, which explores the **exploitation** of the working class and the themes of **poverty** and **class conflict**. The protagonist, **Munoo**, represents the struggles of a young boy migrating from a village to the city in search of a livelihood.
 
• He was one of the founding members of the **Progressive Writers' Association** (PWA) in **1936**, an organization that aimed to use literature as a tool for **social reform** and **political awareness** in pre-independence India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Literary Trio of India:** **Mulk Raj Anand**, along with **R.K. Narayan** and **Raja Rao**, is considered one of the "Big Three" who laid the foundation for the **Indian English Novel**. While Narayan focused on the middle class and Raja Rao on metaphysics, Anand focused on **proletarian** literature.
 
• **Early Life and Education:** Born in **Peshawar** (now in Pakistan), he was educated at **Punjab University** and later earned a **Ph.D.** from **University College London** in **1929**. His stay in **London** brought him into contact with the **Bloomsbury Group**, including authors like **Virginia Woolf** and **E.M. Forster**.
 
• **The Village Trilogy:** He wrote a famous trilogy consisting of **The Village (1939)**, **Across the Black Waters (1940)**, and **The Sword and the Sickle (1942)**. These books trace the life of **Lalu**, a peasant from **Punjab**, and his experiences during **World War I** and the Indian **independence movement**.
 
• **Honors and Awards:** In recognition of his contribution to literature, the **Government of India** awarded him the **Padma Bhushan** in **1967**. He also received the **Sahitya Akademi Award** in **1971** for his novel **The Morning Face**.
 
• **Magazines and Art:** He founded the influential art magazine **Marg** in **1946**, which played a crucial role in promoting **Indian art** and **architecture** to a global audience.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Linguistic Style:** Anand is noted for his unique style of "Indianizing" English. He often translated **Hindi** and **Punjabi** idioms literally into **English** to capture the authentic **flavor** and **rhythm** of **Indian speech**.
 
• **Themes of Social Critique:** His works frequently address **colonialism**, **industrialization**, and the **oppression** of the poor by both the British Raj and the local **bourgeoisie** or **landlord** class.
 
• **Gandhian Influence:** His novel **Untouchable** was famously prefaced by **E.M. Forster**, and Anand himself was deeply influenced by **Mahatma Gandhi**, spending time at **Sabarmati Ashram** to refine his manuscript to better reflect the **realities** of the poor.
